requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
I found no gap. Every obligation maps to marked code and to a test that exercises it.

**Obligations**
1. Every term referenced by the subject or any contributed source contributes its complete fenced declaration, including the phrase option.
2. Definitions referenced by those definitions are included transitively, once each, and cycles terminate.
3. When an additional read introduces a terminology dependency, the same complete, transitive set is supplied to the model and recorded before a submission is accepted.

**Mandatory phase (obligations 1 and 2)**
- `AssessmentSources::prepare` (`src/authoring/inputs.rs`, `{impl}`) builds the contributed selectors: the subject, its cited requirements, impl/test sources and anchors.
- It then calls `definition_inputs` over those inputs plus the subject text, and appends each result only if `mandatory` doesn't already contain it.
- `definition_inputs` (`{impl}`) calls `terms::dependencies`.
  - `direct_references` scans the subject text and each input: Rust comments, Markdown bodies, requirement bodies, and `Definition` selectors.
  - `close_dependencies` expands those terms to a fixed point using a `visited` set and a `BTreeSet`. That gives no duplicates and no nontermination on cycles.
- `source_input` (`{impl}`) turns each term into a `Definition` input. Its text is the whole fenced declaration, with the `:::{definition}` fence and the `:phrase:` line, as the tests below show.

**Additional reads (obligation 3)**
- `read` and `search` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` (`{impl}`) each call `AssessmentSources::additional_definitions`. That runs the same `definition_inputs` closure and filters out definitions already supplied or recorded. The result is returned alongside the read and appended to the delivery's `inputs`.
- In `converse` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`, `{impl}`), delivered inputs go into `pending`. After the next response, `record_inputs` (`{impl}`) records them before any submission is handled, and it deduplicates.
- The `ast_grep` tool the book describes doesn't exist in the code. That gap belongs to `structural_search`, not to this requirement, so I don't count it here.

**Tests**
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` (`src/authoring/inputs.rs`) uses mutually referencing terms `unit` and `value`. It asserts exactly two definition inputs in the mandatory set, which covers transitivity, no duplicates and cycles.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` checks that a term cited from a contributed source becomes a mandatory definition input.
- `definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`) checks a read that introduces a term cycle.
  - It asserts the transitive set `[terms.unit, terms.value]`, once each, in the recorded evidence.
  - It asserts each definition's text starts with `:::{definition}` and `:phrase: `.
  - It asserts the definitions reached the second request, the one before submission, and were absent from the first.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` (`src/authoring/tools.rs`) covers the `habeas` outline read: its result lists `terms.value`, and it is recorded.
- `search_supplies_terminology_clamps_at_eof_and_reports_failures` covers `ripgrep`: the search result carries the definition and it is recorded.

The line-range form of `habeas` calls the same `additional_definitions` without asserting its definitions list. The text doesn't distinguish that path from the others, so it needs no separate test.

When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{req} source_tools
The harness MUST expose a `habeas` tool accepting exactly one of these request
forms. Each form MUST correspond to one existing evidence-input kind:
| Request fields | Evidence input returned | Definition |
| `file: String`, `line_start: Integer`, optional `line_end: Integer` | Outline inputs for the innermost outline nodes covering the range | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `file: String`, `item: String` | Outline input | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `requirements: String` | Requirements input, including its matching names | {cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs` |
| `definition: String` | Definition input | {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` |
Selector arguments MUST use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Reads MUST use the current
project working tree, including unstaged changes to tracked files and staged new
files. By default, source inputs MUST stay within the project root after
resolving symlinks; in a Git worktree, both the requested file and its resolved
target MUST be present in the Git index. Projects outside Git MUST use the same
containment rules without requiring an index. Failure to read an existing
repository's index MUST be reported as an error.
The project-root `evidence/` directory MUST be excluded from model reads by
default, including symlink aliases. Every source the harness supplies to the
model MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. Generated build outputs MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.authoring.generated_inputs`. Workspace path overrides MUST
follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`, including explicit
permission for otherwise excluded inputs. A denied mandatory input or explicit
read MUST abort under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
Line numbers are only a way to request sources; recorded evidence MUST identify
sources by outline selector and structural hash, never by line number. Request
line numbers MUST be one-based and inclusive, and omitting `line_end` MUST read
through EOF. A line-range request MUST be resolved to the innermost outline
nodes covering the requested lines, which are `line` nodes in a file using the
plain-text profile; the result MUST show the model each node's selector, current
line range, and source text, and the harness MUST record those nodes as outline
inputs. The model-facing tool description MUST include the argument conventions
from the cited requirements, including outline selector syntax, definition
selections, and full definition names, with a short request example for each form.
A successful call MUST return the requested evidence input, populated by the
harness with the selected source text, using the existing evidence schema.
{cite}`requirements.ci.schema`

`definitions` MUST be empty when no additional terminology is required. The
